title: AIOS Brain API 1.23 codebase scan payload (POST /api/v1/codebases)
description: Machine-readable contract for the POST /api/v1/codebases request body. Supersedes the 1.22 schema, which it extends with the two optional scanner-identity fields added at document revision 1.23 (AIO-1011): `metrics.scanner_version` and `metrics.scanner_sha`. Strictness is deliberately scoped: `codebase_health` is a closed object (additionalProperties: false, all fields required when present); the surrounding `codebase`/`metrics` shapes stay OPEN to additive scanner-side fields exactly as docs/brain-api.md allows. The full raw-metrics block is required - a sparse health-only payload is invalid here just as the brain rejects it with 422, because the metrics upsert REPLACES the row on (codebase_id, head_sha). LIMIT OF THIS FILE, stated so nobody mistakes green for complete: JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot compare two sibling properties, so the 1.22 CROSS-FIELD invariants (test_coverage_lines_covered <= test_coverage_lines_total; each tests_* part <= tests_total; the parts summing within tests_total; test_coverage_pct agreeing with the counts) are normative in docs/brain-api.md and enforced by the brain, NOT expressible here. What this file does pin - and what it previously did not, letting a payload valid by the canonical contract be 422'd by the brain - is that every one of the six is an integer >= 0 or null. SECOND LIMIT, new at 1.23 and deliberate: the scanner-identity fields are typed loosely (string or null, bounded length) and carry NO `pattern`. Their SHAPE is the scanner's promise, not the brain's gate. A malformed version string must never 422 a scan - a rejected payload drops the repo's whole scan, findings and contributions included, and returns before the ingest run is even logged - so the brain accepts any bounded string and NORMALIZES an unparseable one to the unknown state at read time. Pinning a pattern here would make the canonical contract STRICTER than the implementation, which is the same class of drift as 1.22's looser-than-implementation gap, pointed the other way.

test_coverage_lines_total.description: 1.22. Instrumented lines the coverage report measured - the DENOMINATOR test_coverage_pct was computed over. null = UNKNOWN, never zero and never 'the whole repo'.

test_coverage_lines_covered.description: 1.22. Of test_coverage_lines_total, how many were hit. null = UNKNOWN.

tests_total.description: 1.22. Run integrity: the number of test cases the run collected. null = no test-result report, which is UNKNOWN and must not be read as zero.

tests_passed.description: 1.22. Run integrity: how many passed. null = no test-result report, which is UNKNOWN and must not be read as zero.

tests_skipped.description: 1.22. Run integrity: how many were skipped - non-zero marks the run partial. null = no test-result report, which is UNKNOWN and must not be read as zero.

tests_failed.description: 1.22. Run integrity: how many failed (JUnit failures + errors). null = no test-result report, which is UNKNOWN and must not be read as zero.

scanner_version.description: brain-api 1.23 (AIO-1011). The version of the ingestion package that BUILT this payload - `aios_ingest.__version__`, a dotted semver such as "0.2.0". null or absent = UNKNOWN scanner build, which is what every scan produced before 1.23 reports; it is never read as "current". The brain compares it against the contract's declared `minScannerVersion` (see brain-contract.json's codebasePayloadContract block) to decide whether a repo's scanner predates what the current contract needs, and says so at the point of confusion instead of rendering an unexplained "(scope unknown)". A value the brain cannot parse as a version is treated as unknown, not rejected.

scanner_sha.description: brain-api 1.23 (AIO-1011). PROVENANCE ONLY: the git commit of the aios-team-brain checkout the scanner ran from, when it is knowable - `.github/scripts/fetch-brain-scanner.sh` leaves a real detached checkout at the pinned BRAIN_SHA, so the scanner can read its own build. null when the scanner was installed without git history (a future package install). Never used to compute staleness: commit identity is not ordered, is meaningless across branches, and stops existing the moment the scanner ships as a package. It exists so a stale repo's pin can be located and bumped without guessing.

codebaseHealth.title: codebase_health (document revision 1.15, optional, provenance-only)
codebaseHealth.description: Scalar-only workspace-governance health snapshot, scored scanner-side; the brain persists it verbatim and never recomputes it. All fields are required when the object is present. No file paths, no source text, no contributor identity — failed_invariant_ids are short rubric ids, never paths or findings text.
